pages.text: Mount a $(item)Generator$() on an engine block and the engine also feeds the electrical network it is wired to. It makes power on top of its rotation, at the cost of $(item)torque x0.7$().
$(l)How much$()$(br)Both values follow the engine's speed, the RPM shown on the goggles:$(li)$(item)Voltage = 1.6 V per RPM$()$(li)$(item)Power = 40 W per RPM$()

A type I engine on gasoline at full signal turns at 100 RPM, so its generator gives $(item)160 V and 4000 W$(). A faster engine (turbine, turbo, light fuel) gives more voltage, a slower one less. When the engine stops, so does the power.

Use a $(item)Multimeter$() on the network to read the voltage and power actually generated. Keep an eye on the voltage limit of your cables and machines: most blocks burn out above their maximum voltage (see the Troubleshooting chapter).
